# zanadir

> zanadir is an open-source CLI that reads a repository's CI configuration and reports which security and quality controls are missing, or wired so they cannot fail a build. It answers "what is my pipeline missing?" and "does my CI actually block on security findings?", and prints the CI configuration to add.

- Categories: SCA, Secrets Detection, SAST, Linter, Unit Tests, Coverage, License Compliance, End Of Life, IaC Security, Supply Chain (SBOM, signing, provenance), Workflow Security, Agent Skill Security (scanners for SKILL.md files), Performance Testing.
- Each control found is graded: `enforcing` (can fail a merge), `partial` (runs, but not on every change, e.g. push-only), `advisory` (cannot fail: continue-on-error, `--exit-code 0`, `|| true`, allow_failure, soft-fail flags) or `unknown` (behind a condition the file cannot settle).
- CI platforms: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Bitbucket Pipelines, Azure Pipelines, Jenkins. It follows Makefiles, Taskfiles, tox, goreleaser, go-make, package.json scripts (npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, npm-run-all, turbo, lerna, nx), reusable workflows, local composite actions and CI templates into the commands they run.
- Input: a checkout (`--dir`) or a GitHub repository without cloning (`--repo github.com/owner/name`). Output: table, JSON, SARIF, Markdown.
- `--required-checks` counts a control as enforcing only when branch protection or a ruleset requires its check. `--enforce`, `--fail-on` and `--fail-on-weakened` fail a CI run on gaps.
- It complements OpenSSF Scorecard, which rates project-wide practices through the forge's API; zanadir reads the CI configuration and grades whether each control can fail a build.

For AI coding agents, `zanadir mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server with two read-only tools: `scan` (the JSON report) and `fix` (configuration for the gaps), each taking `dir` (inside the server's `--dir`) or `repo` (anonymous unless the server runs with `--repo-token`). It is listed in the MCP Registry as `io.github.MustacheCase/zanadir`. Add it with `claude mcp add zanadir -- zanadir mcp`, or `{"command": "zanadir", "args": ["mcp"]}` in other clients.

## Usage

```sh
zanadir scan --dir .
zanadir scan --dir . --output json
zanadir scan --repo github.com/owner/name
zanadir scan --dir . --required-checks --fail-on-weakened
zanadir fix --dir .
zanadir fix --dir . --write   # writes .github/workflows/zanadir-suggested.yml
zanadir skills --dir .        # checks the agent skills (SKILL.md) in a checkout
```

Try without installing: `docker run --rm mustachecase/zanadir scan --repo github.com/owner/name`. Install: a prebuilt archive for Linux, macOS or Windows from https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir/releases/latest, `go install github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir@latest`, Homebrew (`brew tap --custom-remote MustacheCase/zanadir https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir.git && brew install mustachecase/zanadir/zanadir`), or the Docker image `mustachecase/zanadir`. In GitHub Actions, use `MustacheCase/zanadir-action`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir/blob/main/README.md): usage, output formats, configuration
- [Effectiveness](https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir/blob/main/README.md#effectiveness): how controls are graded enforcing, partial, advisory or unknown
- [zanadir fix](https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir/blob/main/README.md#zanadir-fix): CI configuration for the gaps
- [zanadir skills](https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir/blob/main/README.md#zanadir-skills): problems in a repository's agent skills
- [Custom rules](https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir/blob/main/README.md#custom-rules): teaching zanadir an in-house tool
- [zanadir-action](https://github.com/MustacheCase/zanadir-action): running zanadir in GitHub Actions
- [State of CI security 2026](https://mustachecase.github.io/state-of-ci/): what the CI of 1,000 of the most-starred GitHub repositories checks, and which checks cannot fail a build
